page: The Vultr voc-g-64c-192gb-960s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform. It delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz, supported by 192.0 GB of system RAM (3.0 GB per vCPU) and a local 960 GB NVMe SSD. The processor features 32 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and hardware cryptography extensions such as AES and VAES.

Benchmark evaluations position this configuration firmly in upper-tier compute and memory performance bands. In multi-threaded execution, stress-ng multi-core testing reached 100,556.13 points, while PassMark CPU achieved 79,514.14 points and PassMark Memory scored in the top 10% at 3,067.69. Large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated uncached read speeds of 340.62 GB/sec and write speeds of 163.16 GB/sec. Data manipulation workloads showed strong efficiency, delivering 87.2 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 384.83 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The 3:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio places this instance between compute-heavy and general-purpose allocations. It provides high CPU parallelism and memory throughput without bundling discrete GPUs. While single-thread benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1,291.0) and single-threaded gzip compression reside in the middle tier due to the 2.0 GHz base frequency, total throughput scales well under concurrent threads. Additionally, CPU-based machine learning inference achieves 53.85 tokens per second for medium 7B model text generation.

This server type is suitable for large-scale enterprise services, including multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput Redis caching, database operations, parallel ETL processing pipelines, and static web serving at scale.

It provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, 192.0 GB of RAM, and 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates modern vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AVX512_BF16. Benchmark testing highlights strong multi-core computational and memory throughput, led by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,067.69 and 87.2 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-core speeds remain average due to the base clock rate, multi-threaded pipelines demonstrate high concurrency across bzip3 compression and clang software builds. Without GPU acceleration, the 3 GB per vCPU allocation provides a balanced profile for concurrent enterprise workloads, making it well-suited for high-traffic web servers, caching layers, database clusters, and multi-threaded compilation systems.
